q: What carbon evidence does EcoVadis ask an Indian supplier for?
title: EcoVadis carbon evidence for suppliers
short: EcoVadis wants documents, not answers alone: a climate or energy policy, Scope 1 and 2 totals with the method used, Scope 3 where you have it, a reduction target, and records of actions taken. Each claim needs a supporting document, and claims without one score little.
audience: Indian exporters rated by EcoVadis for EU and US buyers

sections.h: How EcoVadis scores the carbon part
p: Carbon sits in the Environment theme. EcoVadis scores management systems through indicators such as policies, actions (measures and certifications), how much of the business they cover, and reporting. A policy that exists only in the questionnaire, with no document, is treated much like no policy.

ol: A signed climate or energy policy with a named owner and a date.
A GHG inventory: Scope 1 and Scope 2 totals in tonnes CO2e for a stated year, with the method (GHG Protocol), factors and their sources.
Scope 3 categories you have measured, even if only purchased goods or freight.
A reduction target with a base year and target year, and whether it is validated by SBTi.
Evidence of actions: energy audit reports, solar or efficiency project records, and before and after consumption.
Any public report or sustainability page where the figures appear.

ul: It is dated and covers the period claimed.
It names your company and site, and matches what you wrote in the questionnaire.
Figures trace back to bills and invoices if a reviewer asks.
It covers the whole company or says which sites it leaves out.

sections.h: Common reasons for a low carbon score
ul: Totals with no year or method.
A target with no base year.
Actions described in words with no records.
Data for one site presented as the whole company.

senseible: Senseible reads electricity bills, fuel and purchase invoices into a Scope 1, 2 and 3 record with the source document behind each line, which you can attach as evidence. Its reports are self-declared drafts, and the EcoVadis rating itself comes from EcoVadis.
